To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a high-efficiency, double-doped electrophosphorescence white organic light-emiting diode.
the white electrophosphorescence with a high power efficiency of 10.7 cd A−1 is obtained from a device with a double-dopant emissive layer, in which Ir(piq) 2(acac) is codoped with Ir(ppy) 3 in TPBI.
a double-doped electrophosphorescence device with a white emission is reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of high efficiency white organic light emitting devices by doping two different dopants into a single host material, TPBI.
the fabrication and optimization of a white electrophosphorescence device with a high efficiency and high colour rendering index.
the development of a highly efficient, stable, and colour-tunable white organic light-emiting device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the device with 4 wt% of Ir(ppy)2(acac)/Ir(piq)3 in the TPBI host is the best device with a maximum luminance of 33 000 and power efficiency of 10.7 cd A−1 and 10.1 lm W−1 at 1000 cd m−2.
the device has a high power efficiency of 10.7lm W−1, a high luminous efficacy of 24.3 lm W−1 at 1000 cd m−2, a low turn on voltage of 4 V and a CIE coordinate of (0.29; 0.34).
this paper describes a new approach for efficient white OLEDs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the white emission from the double-doped electrophosphorescence devices can be achieved by mixing red and green emissions from the Ir(piq) 2(acac)–TPBI and Ir(ppy ) 3–TPBI systems, respectively.
the double-doped electrophosphorescence devices with the TPBI host are promising for the fabrication of high-efficiency white organic light-emission devices with good colour stability.
the double-doped emissively layer is a good candidate for white organic light-emitted diodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high-efficiency, white electrophosphorescence device is demonstrated by using a single host with a double emissive layer.
the use of a single host material for codoping two dopants is an effective way to achieve white emission.
